question: What can the engineer system do that LLMs cannot, that we have not already implemented?

gap_list.title: Machine-checked proofs (Lean/Coq/Isabelle kernel)
gap_list.why_not_llm: LLMs can sketch proofs; cannot guarantee kernel acceptance

gap_list.title: Bit-exact multi-run replay under pinned RNG+deps
gap_list.why_not_llm: LLMs are stochastic; no bit-exact artifact replay

gap_list.title: SMT/SAT checks on constraint sets before decide
Interval/affine arithmetic for rigorous numeric bounds
Merkle/hash chain over full artifact tree per run
Continuous fuzzing of engineer gates with mutating inputs
gap_list.why_not_llm: Systematic mutation testing vs prompt sampling

gap_list.title: OS-level CPU/mem/time sandbox on non-stationary probes
gap_list.why_not_llm: Enforcement is OS/runtime, not text generation

gap_list.title: Typed intermediate representation for actions before execution sim
gap_list.why_not_llm: Type soundness proofs vs free-form JSON

gap_list.title: Explicit causal graph + d-separation checks on features
gap_list.why_not_llm: Graph criteria are mechanical; LLMs confabulate causality

gap_list.title: Read-only chain observer with availability timestamps
gap_list.why_not_llm: Grounded external state vs parametric memory

stationary_note: Engineers excel at fail-closed mechanical verification, provenance, and deterministic gates. LLMs excel at open-ended language and hypothesis generation. The spine uses LLMs only after gates; gaps below are non-LLM strengths not yet built.
